_description: The model version identifier (IP-unified-architecture §10). MAJOR = structural change (a law, a divisor set, H). MINOR = refit (coefficients move, structure does not). Deliberately OUTSIDE model-parameters.json: a version label must not change the model's content identity (CONSTANTS_HASH). Seeded at v10.0 continuing the repo's existing v9/v10 tag lineage (owner decision); MAJOR/MINOR bumps proceed from here under this scheme. Content identity is carried separately by CONSTANTS_HASH (model parameters) and COEFFICIENTS_HASH (the fit) in packages/physics/src/constants/.
_v26_4Note: v26.3 → v26.4 (the small-remainders batch and plan 13's leftovers): a MINOR — coefficients move, structure does not. The browser's climate coefficients (public/input/climate-formula-coefficients.json) are a FIT of the proxy records on the L1 line set, and the shipped file had stayed at the previous fit after v26.2 re-derived the line set (up to 1.8e-3 relative in the ridge coefficients — a near-degenerate basis; the stitched curves themselves move far less): re-exported, and the export is now GOVERNED (an inputs block, REQUIRED by check:artifacts, a regen:cascade node — the cascade scans public/input/ too), as is the L1 line audit whose labels reach the paper. The L1 lines carry Laskar's mode names (the chain artifact records the ONE Laskar 2004 reference table; the T1 export labels each mode by its nearest reference within 0.05 ″/yr; a line is g₄−g₅, g₃−g₁, z₅−g₂ … — the former labels were the mode table's own indices). The ΔT stack re-closed on the corrected coefficients: deltaTStart 56.0758 s unchanged at four decimals, every coefficient within 4e-8 relative except the degenerate resonator kick pair (1e-5); the fitter's own _meta/config restated without the deleted lattice framing. Registry: generalPrecessionIau2006ArcsecPerCy / ArcsecPerYr (read from the plan-09 input p_A — the model's p₀ IS p_A), moonKeplerSiderealMonthDays / moonKeplerDayLengthSeconds / moonKeplerEarthMassFraction (the GM chain's inputs, so two pages' computation blocks are value tags); knownValues.generalPrecessionArcsecCy and mainstreamAxialPrecExactYr left astro-reference (derived). The tools/lib and browser goldens re-recorded (the GIA α channel's rows at 1e-5, the cardinal instants and positions at 1e-9 — the corrected climate coefficients through α(t) → ΔT). Same batch: the browser's 311 unit literals read SECONDS_PER_DAY / DAYS_PER_JULIAN_YEAR (proven bit-identical on the shipped constants), the plan-13 doc-stripping pass (docs 11/20/21/40/41/65/66/99/104). @essrt/physics 23.3.0, @essrt/model-values 24.3.0.

_v26_2Note: v26.1 → v26.2 (plan 12 §8, option (a) — the mean obliquity of date is a CITED INPUT): a MINOR — no coefficient moved, no law changed; one factor the composed law had held at J2000 now rides the cited history. The composed lunisolar law ψ̇ = [ω/ω₀]·p₀·[f_S + (1 − f_S)(a₀/a_M)³] scales the precession CONSTANT α(t); the precession RATE is α(t)·cos ε̄(t), and the chain had held cos ε̄ at its J2000 value at every epoch (a purity freeze without its twin). Standard theory (Goldreich 1966; Touma & Wisdom 1994; Farhat et al. 2022) has the mean obliquity lower in the deep past, evolved by the lunar tidal torque — the same ocean-dissipation physics option A declined to model — so, as the distance is, Farhat et al. 2022's own mean-obliquity column of the SAME cited table (data/astrogeo22-earth-moon.json, embedded with the distance) is the input, read as the shape cos ε̄(t)/cos ε̄(0) (earth/mean-obliquity-history). MEASURED: the factor is 1 − 2e-7 at 10 kyr (the ΔT era moves ≤ 3.4e-7 s), 1.0075 at the Devonian, 1.0245 at 2.46 Ga; the published clock T_p moves 21,396 → 21,235 yr (Devonian) and 12,154 → 11,863 yr (2.46 Ga); the composed rate closes to Farhat's own precession column (−2.0 % → +0.4 % at 2.46 Ga) and every paleo precession referee moves toward its source — Lantink 2460 −1.8 → +0.6 %, Xiamaling 1400 −1.0 → +0.9 %, Zhou Yemahe −3.5 → −1.8 %, Wumishan −6.5 → −4.8 %, Chuanlinggou −7.2 → −5.3 % (the Mesoproterozoic discrepancy HALVED, not closed; the bands restated with the cause). TWO rates now, named: lunisolarTorqueRate… (the constant's scaling, what the hybrid obliquity integration takes — its own ŝ·n̂ carries the cosine — and the realized pole-rate window mean the climate lines ride, both bit-identical) and lunisolarPrecessionRate… (the rate of date: T_p(t), the obliquity beat, the tropical year of date, the paleo rows). SECOND CHANGE, measured on the way (§8.3): the hybrid's ζ-mode tail beyond the banked series' ±10 Myr was anchored to the J2000 POINT and reached the span edges 1.6°/0.7° away from the series, kicking the hybrid's mean obliquity +0.9°/+0.3° for the whole deep tail (24.17° at −20 Myr against 23.3° inside); the tail now joins the series at each seam (n̂ continuous; ε step +0.09°/+0.13°, the tail's mean 23.31–23.36° over ±100 Myr). The hybrid still carries NO tidal evolution of the mean beyond the span — the cited mean obliquity of date is published beside it (model.earth.meanObliquityCitedDeg, the API's /earth payload). Fixtures and goldens re-recorded at the ppm class beyond ±10 kyr; the historical era at 1e-7. @essrt/physics 23.2.0, @essrt/model-values 24.2.0.

_v26Note: v25.0 → v26.0 (plan 12, option A — the Earth–Moon distance history is a CITED PHYSICAL INPUT): a structural MAJOR. The model cannot derive the Moon's recession history (it needs an ocean-dissipation history it has no physics for), so a(t) is Farhat, Auclair-Desrotour, Boué & Laskar 2022's published solution (the AstroGeo22 ephemeris, data/astrogeo22-earth-moon.json, 0–4,429 Ma at 1 Myr), read as the ratio a(t)/a(0) on the model's own observed J2000 distance with the LLR rate as the J2000 slope (packages/physics deltat/moon-distance-history). Everything downstream is derived by the model's equations — the day length by angular-momentum conservation with the J2000 L_EM constant, the composed precession and the clock, the month chain — and every rock datum is a TEST (the paleo gate: 45 rows, each tolerance or band written with its cause; Zhou 2024's three precession constants join as the measured quantity; the Mesoproterozoic 2.5–3.6σ gap is the stated open discrepancy). DELETED: the quartic's α₃/α₄ (a two-coefficient copy of the same curve), the Driver-1½ regime block (knots fitted to the rock record) and its two fitters, the solar-channel budget and the thermal-tide pump, the Roche-crossing 'self-validation' at 4.498 Ga (the spline's pinned endpoint; the genesis is the input's end, 4.429 Ga) — and the circularity in which Xiamaling and Joffre were fit anchors and falsification tests at once. Measured: J2000 and the LLR tidal rate bit-identical; 380 Ma LOD 21.76 vs 21.92 h; the ΔT era moves 0.2 s at 0 AD and 1.8 s at −2000 because the cited history's mean recession over its first Myr (3.833 cm/yr) differs from the pinned LLR slope (3.820) and the smooth join bends — the ΔT stack is re-closed in this version and the eclipse and lunar records rebaselined with that explanation. @essrt/physics 23.0.0, @essrt/model-values 24.0.0.

_v23Note: v22.0 → v23.0 (the realized obliquity period): a structural MAJOR — the obliquity lines' rate convention changes again, from the J2000 instant to the window mean. MEASURED FIRST: the dominant obliquity line of the model's OWN ε(t), fitted over the LR04 window (0–5.32 Ma) with the full line set p + sᵢ and one free p, sits at 40,922 yr — not at the J2000 beat 41,098 (v22.0) nor at the general-rate beat 41,224 (v21.0) — and La2004's own series on the same fit reads 40,900 (Zeebe & Lantink's ZB18a FFT over 6 Myr: 40,900); the two integrations agree at every window (2 Myr 41,087 / 41,080; 3 Myr 41,003 / 40,990; 5 Myr 40,938 / 40,917; 5.32 Myr 40,922 / 40,900). The pole turned faster in the past: the window mean of the rate the spin integration actually turns the pole at — the inertial secular rate of date × the solar-torque factor at e(t) × J₂(t)/J₂₀ × cos ε(t)/cos ε₀ (ds/dt = α(ŝ·n̂)(ŝ×n̂): the azimuthal rate about n̂ is α cos ε) — reads 50.515 ″/yr over the record against 50.385 at J2000 (tidal spin +0.06, lower mean obliquity +0.05, higher mean eccentricity +0.015), and predicts the fitted period to 0.02 % (40,930 against the fitted 40,922). The climate records had said the same: the clock test's preferred '+0.12…+0.20 ″/yr on the obliquity lines' (full record 50.505 against the window mean 50.515; pre-iNHG 50.585 against 50.560) was this window mean, not a free offset. ONE home: createModel().lunisolar.spinAxisInertialRateMeanArcsecPerYr(yearFrom, yearTo) and obliquityPeriodRealizedYears(yearFrom, yearTo); the J2000 beat (obliquityBeatYearsAtYear, obliqCycleYears, 41,098) stays as the instantaneous limit. The T1 exporter writes the realized rate over the LR04 window (the stack's own span, the ONE home of the window) and scripts/l1_physical_lines.py derives the ten obliquity lines on it (41.10 → 40.92 kyr for p+s₀ and the others in proportion); the climatic-precession lines keep the general precession (the records resolve no offset there). LOOP TRAP measured on the way: the J₂(t)/J₂₀ factor is the ice-driven GIA channel, which rides the climate formula's own post-MPT layer — a line rate on the full physics depends on its own fit (1.4e-3 ″/yr in the factor's window mean and 1.8e-3 in ⟨cos ε⟩ across one refit, a loop the freshness gate cannot close). The lines are therefore derived on the ORBITAL FORCING ALONE: a second model built with createModel opts.giaEllipticityOfDate = false (no J₂(t) factor in the integration), whose window mean reads 50.519 ″/yr and is stable across a refit to 1e-4; the published realized period and the hybrid verdict's gate keep the full physics (50.516, 2–3 yr of period apart). The forcing lines must not contain the climate response. GATE: the obliquity-hybrid verdict now fits the realized period of the shipped model's ε(t) and REFUSES if it parts from the window-mean prediction by more than 0.1 % (fail-proven via ESSRT_OBLIQ_REALIZED_PLANT=1); La2004's fit rides beside it as the theory label (registry obliqCycleRealized*/obliqCycleLa2004FitLr04Years/obliqCycleRealizedVsLa2004Pct). The published convergence statement is like for like again: the model's realized period against La2004's on the same window and fit (0.05 %), where v22.0 had compared a J2000 beat with a long-window precession frequency (Laskar's 50.476 is a precession frequency of his solution, not a J2000 rate). THE CASCADE as in v22.0: the climate formula refit on the new lines, the GIA α(t) channel, the precession-of-date J₂(t) factor and the ΔT stack (Step 7c re-closed), the eclipse-audit and lunar-alignment records re-baselined, the goldens re-recorded. Packages: @essrt/physics 20.0.0, @essrt/model-values 19.0.0.
_v22Note: v21.0 → v22.0 (the lunisolar anchor of the obliquity lines): a structural MAJOR — a line convention changes, and the published obliquity period with it. The climate formula's obliquity lines p + sᵢ had been derived on the general precession in longitude p₀ = 50.288 ″/yr (the model's J2000 precession reading, the equinox along the ecliptic of date) like the climatic-precession lines p + gᵢ. An obliquity line is the spin axis precessing in the INERTIAL frame against one of the ecliptic's nodal modes, so it carries the spin axis's inertial rate — the self-anchored rate the hybrid obliquity integration already integrated ŝ on (earth/deep-orbital-history, D4e: the general precession plus the planetary mean the N-body ecliptic's motion carries): 50.385 ″/yr at J2000 in the shipped, series-driven configuration (period 25,722 yr; the +0.097 is IAU's planetary precession ψ_A − p_A; La2004's precession frequency 50.476 sits 0.09 above). TRAP MEASURED: a bare createModel() (the 18-term mode table) anchors the spin axis 0.18 ″/yr above p₀ — the first derivation ran on it and read 50.469, 40,986 yr; derive line rates in the shipped configuration (pass secularSeriesArtifact), the g₂-gap trap in a new coat. MEASURED FIRST (doc 99, the clock-of-date test with its three controls): on the old lines every LR04 window asked for a constant +0.20…+0.30 ″/yr on the p-lines and the per-family scan put the whole gain in the obliquity family (+0.018 / +0.089 / +0.136 ΔR² in iNHG-MPT / pre-iNHG / full LR04), the climatic-precession family wanting none; the untuned Cheng 2016 record asked for the same direction. The rate is now exported (createModel().lunisolar.spinAxisInertialRateArcsecPerYrJ2000 / …PeriodYearsJ2000 / …RateArcsecPerYrAtYear), the T1 exporter writes it beside p, and scripts/l1_physical_lines.py derives the ten obliquity lines on it: 41.22 → 41.10 kyr (p+s₀), 39.84 → 39.72, 40.52 → 40.40, 41.96 → 41.82, 54.13 → 53.92, 27.40 → 27.35, 28.99 → 28.93, 29.16 → 29.09, 29.77 → 29.71, 29.97 → 29.90; the eccentricity and climatic-precession lines are unchanged.
